newsitem.title: THAILAND: Data show shaky Thai economy gaining stability.
newsitem.headline: Data show shaky Thai economy gaining stability.

text.p: The Thai central bank said on Thursday that the sluggish economy had become more stable in December and January but noted there were no clear signs that slowdowns in investment and industry had bottomed out.

Bank of Thailand chief economist Kleothong Hetrakul told a news conference that narrowing trade and current account deficits in December confirmed the growing stability of the economy after a sharp slackening due to weak exports in 1996.
"Every indicator pointed to improving stability...the current account figure showed that it was going in the direction that we would like to see," she said.

The bank said the December current account deficit narrowed for the third straight month, to a 15-month low of 19.1 billion baht ($735 million) from 21.7 billion in November and 31.7 billion a year ago.
It said the December trade deficit also fell to 22.3 billion baht from 24.2 billion in November and 29.4 billion a year ago.
Olarn Chaipravat, president of the Thai Bankers Association, welcomed the development.
"The Thai economy has moved out of its high current account deficit crisis," he said, referring to its peak last April when the account showed a 49.6 billion baht monthly deficit.
But Kleothong agreed with private analysts that anemic economic activity since mid-1996 was little changed.
She said the private investment index posted a 7.5 percent year-on-year growth in December against 7.7 percent the previous month and 14.3 percent a year ago.
The central bank official said private businesses continued trimming investment in machinery and capital goods in December.

The December industrial output index rose 4.8 percent year- on-year against 4.1 percent in November but Kleothong attributed the modest improvement to the start of annual domestic sugar production season during the month.

Analysts said for the economy to return to the previous pace of expansion seen during the first half of the 1990s, private investment and industrial production should both show at least double digit year-on-year growth.

They said another indicator of weak economic conditions was a sustained decline of commercial bank lending. Total outstanding loans extended by banks grew 13.7 percent year-on-year in January, their smallest rise in at least several years and against 19.0 percent a year ago.
Kleothong declined to forecast when the economy may pick up. "We are going through an adjustment period and the central bank will monitor the situation closely," she said.

She said, however, that the government sector performed better in January and the country's balance of payments ended the month with a healthy 24.7 billion baht surplus after two months of rare deficits.
The bank economist said the January surplus was helped by a net capital inflow of over 10 billion baht in the month.
